studyStatus: Exploratory experiment designed AFTER observing 16 invalid static plans among 18 fixed disruption checks. Not part of the main 48-case preregistered benchmark; not an independently preregistered discovery claim.
scenarioSource: makeStressScenario(seed) exported from scripts/robustness-v2.mjs; exact same six root scenarios
baselineSource: Saved complete initialPlan from data/robustness-v2.json; no reselection or rerun of original plans

bufferRule.otherInputs: Keep release days, due days, warehouse capacity, staging capacity, return lag, tariff and horizon unchanged. Buffer does not know which boxes or days will be disrupted.

uncertaintyEnvelope: Each box's actual unloading duration is between its nominal duration and nominal+1 day; each day's actual truck capacity is at least max(0, nominal-2); all other modeled inputs are unchanged. No guarantee outside this explicit envelope or beyond the static daily model.
audits: Independently audit the conservative schedule under full-buffer worst-case durations/capacity, original nominal inputs, and the three fixed root disruptions. Use actual durations in each audit, never trust saved unloadEndDay. Pickup/unload-start/return dates remain fixed in all checks.
cost: Recompute nominal complete two-fee cost with original tariff at conservative planned pickup/return dates. Compare to saved original complete feasible plan; report total and incremental absolute/pct additional cost, denominator named. Exclude no case silently. Null or zero denominator produces null percent. Do not compare incomplete schedules.
reporting: Retain infeasible and timeout cases; report feasible/optimal counts and paired cost premiums only for complete feasible original and conservative plans. Three disturbances reuse each scenario, so no random failure rate or independent-sample interval. This is a static buffer tradeoff, not online rolling recovery.
